title: Derived pullback commutes with derived tensor product on the constructible categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the coefficient categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with the finite bounded constructible category of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the derived-complete integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and arbitrary $M,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
 \mu_{f;M,N}:Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*N
$$
in the ambient derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$. In particular this applies to $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$, without asserting that their derived tensor product is bounded.

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ and $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, the same formula is an isomorphism in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$; the integral tensor product is the completed derived tensor product specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At finite level $\mu$ is the canonical tensor comparison for the morphism of ringed topoi induced by $f$. At integral level it is the functorial derived inverse limit of the finite comparisons on $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and $N_n=N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, using the canonical reduction identifications for completed pullback and tensor. At rational level it is the image of the integral comparison; at the $\Qlb$ level it is represented by the rational comparison over any common finite coefficient field, composed with the scalar-extension comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

These isomorphisms are natural in $M,N$, compatible with associativity, the signed commutativity and the unit isomorphisms of derived tensor, and compatible with composition: for $h:Z\to X$, $\mu_{f\circ h;M,N}$ is $\mu_{h;Lf^*M,Lf^*N}\circ Lh^*(\mu_{f;M,N})$ under the canonical composition identifications of pullbacks. They commute with finite reduction (including the derived change of coefficients $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$ for $m\geq n$) and with scalar extension through finite coefficient field extensions and into $\Qlb$.

source.place: Lemma 21.18.4 (Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product), for the morphism of ringed topoi (X_proet, (A_{E,n})_X) -> (Y_proet, (A_{E,n})_Y); the integral, rational and Qlbar levels follow the level-by-level definitions of the operations in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom

proof.text: At finite level choose compatible small representatives of the pro-etale sites as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The inverse image and its constant-ring map make $f_n$ a morphism of ringed topoi. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], module pullback is exact and agrees with inverse image with the coefficient action transported through $f^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y\cong(A_{E,n})_X$. Thus its derived functor is precisely the finite operation in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with $R=(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $S=(A_{E,n})_X$. Its displayed isomorphism, natural in both arguments, is $\mu_{f;M,N}$. That theorem is unbounded, so it applies to all the finite-level inputs claimed here; no finite Tor dimension of $A_{E,n}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), applied to the small pro-etale ringed topoi

proof.text: Check the finite comparison and its coherences on K-flat resolutions $P,Q$ with flat terms, supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Tensor totals stay in the resolving class: for an acyclic test complex $H$, the total of $H\otimes(P\otimes Q)$ identifies, by reindexing the direct sums and the signed differentials, with the total of $(H\otimes P)\otimes Q$; it is acyclic by K-flatness twice [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Each $P^p\otimes Q^q$ is flat because tensoring with it is a composite of two exact tensor functors, and the countable sums in each total degree are flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. Thus iterated tensors below compute the iterated derived tensors. The comparison is obtained by totalizing the module comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]: in extension-of-scalars notation its degree-$(p,q)$ map is $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, with inverse $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)\mapsto st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. These are balanced maps of sheaves. The total differential is $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], so both maps commute with it. For three homogeneous factors, both associativity paths send $s\otimes((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ to $(s\otimes x)\otimes((1\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes z))$. Both symmetry paths introduce the same $(-1)^{pq}$ and interchange $x,y$; both unit paths multiply the scalar coefficient. For $h:Z\to X$, the inverse-image composition identification comes from the adjunctions of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: the two right adjoints evaluate on canonically identical iterated fibre products, so their left adjoints have the unique adjunction-compatible identification. After this identification both tensor-composition paths have the displayed formula with the same coefficient $s$ in the final ring. Finally, for a coefficient map $A\to B$, the two change-of-rings paths both take $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$; this includes all quotient maps and their composites. Equalities on these pure tensors give equalities on the sheaf tensor products and hence on their direct-sum totals. The resolving-class equivalence and uniqueness of extension in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] descend the maps and these equalities, one variable at a time, to arbitrary derived inputs. This proves finite associativity, signed symmetry, unit, composition and coefficient compatibility, rather than assuming that naturality alone supplies them.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), its total-complex construction; Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); explicit tensor identities

proof.text: For integral $M,N$, choose K-flat resolutions $P,Q$ with flat terms over $R_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and put $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $Q_n=Q\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] these are K-flat with flat terms. Use the actual quotient chain maps of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], not merely inverse systems in the homotopy category. Set $T_n=\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}Q_n)$, $U_n=f_n^*P_n$, $V_n=f_n^*Q_n$ and $W_n=\operatorname{Tot}(U_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}V_n)$. The $U_n,V_n$ are K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. All four are coherent towers of the kind in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]: for $m\geq n$, associating ordinary quotient tensors identifies $P_m\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}A_{E,n}$ with $P_n$, and likewise for $Q$; step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], also applied to the identity topos and the ring map $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$, give the corresponding normalization isomorphisms for $T,U,V,W$. The chain maps are induced by quotient homomorphisms, whose composites are the direct quotients, so the normalization cocycles and strict tower data are present. By [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] the derived limits of these towers have canonically and coherently these finite reductions. In particular the reductions of $M\widehat\otimes^L N$, $Lf^*M$ and $Lf^*N$ are $T_n,U_n,V_n$, respectively, with their quotient maps.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); coherent quotient towers and normalized DVR effectivity

proof.text: The degreewise comparison of step 2 gives a strict isomorphism of the towers $f_n^*T_n\to W_n$: the maps and their inverses commute with all quotient transitions by the same tensor formula. Restrict scalars to $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and apply the functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)))\to D(R_X)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. A functor carries an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse maps. Here the identifications with the composite operations use whole coherent reduction towers. Put $K=R\lim T_\bullet$, $F=R\lim U_\bullet$ and $G=R\lim V_\bullet$. The canonical coherent counits in [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], used in step 3, identify the reduction towers of $K,F,G$ with $T_\bullet,U_\bullet,V_\bullet$, respectively. Apply finite pullback to the first coherent comparison; its exactness from step 1 gives the comparison of pullback towers. Apply finite derived tensor to the latter two comparisons, computed using their flat-term K-flat representatives from step 3; this gives the comparison of tensor towers with $W_\bullet$. These are coherent comparisons in the derived tower categories, so applying $R\lim$ gives the identifications with $Lf^*K$ and $F\widehat\otimes^L G$ prescribed by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Consequently the source is $Lf^*(M\widehat\otimes^L N)$ and the target is $Lf^*M\widehat\otimes^L Lf^*N$; these identifications do not use independently chosen levelwise isomorphisms. This defines the integral $\mu$ and proves that it is the derived limit stipulated in the statement. Its construction on representatives descends naturally and independently of resolutions by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Finally [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] puts both source and target in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$: apply its tensor assertion on $Y$, its pullback assertion, and its tensor assertion on $X$ to the two pulled-back objects. Since this is a full subcategory, the ambient isomorphism and its inverse belong to it.

proof.text: The integral coherences are images of coherent tower diagrams, not conclusions inferred merely from equality of isolated reduction maps. For example, resolve three inputs by $P,Q,H$. At index $n$ the two associativity paths are exactly the two triple-tensor maps computed in step 2; their equality is compatible with the transition $n+1\to n$, since that transition applies the coefficient quotient to each displayed scalar. For signed symmetry, a homogeneous tensor $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$, with degrees $p,q$, is sent by either path to $(-1)^{pq}(s\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes x)$; the coefficient quotient changes $s$ but neither degree nor sign, so this equality is an equality of maps of towers. For the unit, the two paths both multiply the coefficient by the unit-factor scalar; quotient homomorphisms preserve that multiplication and $1$. For composition, the coherent reduction of $Lh^*Lf^*M$ is $h_n^*f_n^*M_n$; the adjunction-compatible finite identification with $(f\circ h)_n^*M_n$ from step 2 identifies both composite tensor maps at the level of these coherent quotient models: each distributes $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ as $(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ after the iterated inverse images are identified. For the transition from index $n+1$ to $n$, each factor is reduced by the coefficient quotient, so distributing before or after that transition has the identical displayed value. Thus the composition equality also holds as a map of towers. Apply the functor in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to these diagrams and use the canonical coherent counit comparisons of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. This gives the integral associativity, symmetry, unit and composition equations. Applying the same counit comparisons to the strict map $f_n^*T_n\to W_n$ identifies its derived reduction with the finite $\mu_{f_n;M_n,N_n}$, proving compatibility with finite reduction. This uses the coherent normalization in step 3, with no claim that separate finite-reduction functors are faithful on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); canonical coherent reduction counits; tensor identities of step 2

proof.text: Let $E\subset L$ be finite coefficient fields and write $B_m=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$. By [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] the maps $A_{E,m}\to B_m$ exist and commute with transitions, even for ramified extensions; scalar extension is the derived limit of the strict towers $P\otimes_{R_Y}(B_m)_Y$. For normalization, the change-of-rings lemma used in step 3 makes each quotient complex $P\otimes_{R_Y}(B_m)_Y$ K-flat with flat terms over $B_m$. Derived change of rings along $B_m\to B_n$ is consequently computed by ordinary tensor on that quotient complex. Associating the two tensors identifies it with $P\otimes_{R_Y}(B_n)_Y$. The transition is induced by the actual quotient $B_m\to B_n$, and two successive quotient maps equal the direct quotient, giving the normalization cocycle. Hence [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] for the coefficient field $L$ supplies the coherent reductions of the limit. The existence of natural pullback and tensor scalar-extension isomorphisms, with identity and composition compatibility, is supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Choose their canonical quotient-model representatives as follows. For any derived-complete object $K$, associate derived change of rings through $A_{E,m}$ and use its coherent reduction counit to identify the $B_m$ reduction after scalar extension with $K_m\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m$. For pullback, apply the finite change-of-rings formula of step 2 to identify this model for $Lf_E^*K$ with $f_L^*(K_m\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m)$. For tensor, that formula identifies $(M_m\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}N_m)\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m$ with $(M_m\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m)\otimes^L_{B_m}(N_m\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m)$. The quotient formulas commute with transitions, so their derived limits give the indicated comparison isomorphisms; the formulas for the identity ring map and a composite ring map give their identity and composition compatibility. To check compatibility of $\mu$ with these comparisons, compute using the indicated quotient models: the $B_m$ model of the first input is $P_m\otimes_{A_{E,m}}B_m$ and the $B_m$ model of the second input is $Q_m\otimes_{A_{E,m}}B_m$, by tensor associativity. The $B_m$ models of the two tensor/pullback paths are identified by the change-of-rings formulas of step 2; both take $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. These formulas commute with $B_{m+1}\to B_m$ and also with any further coefficient extension. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to the resulting commuting diagrams of quotient towers gives the integral scalar-extension compatibility square for $\mu$. The coherent counit comparisons identify the vertices with the integral operations, as in step 4. Thus the calculation checks the comparisons used by the coefficient constructions, and does not deduce a compatibility assertion solely from the existence of some scalar-extension isomorphisms.

source.place: Compatible quotient scalar-extension construction of def-weil-integral-scalar-extension; Tag 07A4 tensor formula and Tag 0941 functorial derived limit

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], every rational object is an integral object and every morphism is a finite sum of $u\otimes a$, with $u$ integral and $a\in E$. Define $\mu^E$ to be the image $\mu^{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$; its inverse is the image of the integral inverse. The operations on rational morphisms are the scalar extensions specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The integral naturality identity for $u,v$, multiplied by the corresponding scalars, gives rational naturality; add the resulting identities for sums. Every integral coherence equation remains an equality after tensoring Hom groups with $E$, so the rational associativity, symmetry, unit and composition equations follow. The scalar-extension square of step 6 likewise remains commutative, since the rational scalar-extension functor is the one induced from the integral scalar-extension functor.

source.place: The raw scalar-localization definition: Hom tensor E; all identities are images of the integral identities

proof.text: For objects $(E,M),(E',N)$ at the algebraically closed level, choose a common finite coefficient field $L$ and form the rational comparison there, conjugated by the scalar-extension comparisons as prescribed in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Represent the inverse by the inverse rational comparison with the inverse conjugating comparisons. In [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], morphisms are classes over common finite fields, and two representatives agree if they agree after passage to a further common field. Step 6 after rationalization says precisely that passing from $L$ to any larger field sends this comparison to the same comparison there; hence the class and its inverse are independent of $L$. Represent any finite naturality or coherence diagram over a single common finite field; the rational identity proved in step 7 gives its equality in the colimit Hom group. This proves all the asserted compatibilities at $\Qlb$, including scalar extension into $\Qlb$.

split_report.summary: Corrected the false finite-level boundedness assertion, retaining the tensor/pullback isomorphism for all ambient finite-level complexes and all original integral/rational/common-stage clauses. Gave eight steps using existing ringed-topos and normalized-tower statements, including explicit tensor identities for coherence and functorial derived-limit maps. No new nodes. Checked sources, existing Lean, all cited statements, ramified coefficient changes, and the sole citer (which uses only E and Qlbar). Resumption audit made tensor-total K-flatness explicit from the definition and cited flatness of countable sums, added direct change-of-rings citations to step 6, and restored proposed generic tool uses in the authorized split_report field. Fresh second reading clarified the coherent tower identifications for composite integral operations in step 4, added its direct effectivity citation, and independently repeated Mathlib searches with different vocabulary.

Generic resolving-class localization descends natural transformations and their identities from K-flat models; the conventions unit has no localization theorem.
Generic K-flat and flat-term preservation permits the finite pullback models; no geometric argument is replaced.

The derived-limit functor on coherent strict towers gives actual maps and preserves diagram identities, which the Roos-triangle definition alone does not supply.
Generic normalized DVR tower effectivity supplies coherent reductions of completed operations; it does not replace the unit route or assume constructibility.
Generic flat-term K-flat resolutions on ringed sites supply representatives; the conventions unit has no resolution construction.
Only the generic clause that countable sums of flat sheaves are flat is used for the terms of a tensor total; K-flatness of that total is proved directly from the definition in step 2.
